property_summary: For any owner and any proposed address, a successful call to setOwner(newOwner) must make c.owner() equal newOwner; the mutant never updates owner, so it violates this for any newOwner different from the current owner.
For any fuzzed address a, a successful ownership transfer to a followed by a call to setOwner from a must succeed, but the mutant never changes owner so a is not owner and the second call reverts.
For any caller who is the current owner, setOwner(newOwner) must set owner to exactly the supplied newOwner; the mutant instead sets owner to msg.sender, violating this for any newOwner != caller.
For any new owner address passed by the current owner, setOwner must make c.owner() equal that address; the mutant returns early so owner never changes, breaking this for some fuzzed address.
The current owner can always change ownership: calling setOwner from the address returned by c.owner() must succeed and update owner, but the mutant inverts onlyOwner so the owner's call reverts.

Only the current owner can change `owner`: after any call to setOwner by a non-owner actor, c.owner() is unchanged; the mutant lets any non-zero caller overwrite it, so for some actor != owner the owner differs.

For every admissible caller that is neither the current owner nor the zero address, calling setOwner must revert (the owner restriction holds); the mutant, which only checks msg.sender != address(0), lets such a caller succeed and overwrite owner.
For any caller and any address, a setOwner call by the current owner that completes must return true (and update the owner); the mutant returns false, breaking this for every successful call.

For any caller who is the current owner and any address, a successful call to setOwner always returns true; the mutant omits 'return true', so the named return stays false and violates this rule for every input.
For any caller that is not the current owner, a call to setOwner must revert and leave c.owner() unchanged; the mutant lets any caller succeed, so c.owner() changes.

Only the current owner can change ownership: for any caller that is not the owner, setOwner must revert and leave owner unchanged; the mutant removed the onlyOwner guard so any caller succeeds and owner changes.

For any fuzzed candidate address _owner, a setOwner call made by the current owner must return successfully and set owner() exactly to _owner; the mutant instead stores address(0), so owner() != _owner whenever _owner != address(0).
For any caller equal to the owner and any new owner address, a successful call to setOwner must return true and update the owner state; the mutant returns false without changing owner.

For any caller and any address argument, calling setOwner(newOwner) must make c.owner() equal exactly newOwner; the mutant ignores the argument and sets owner to msg.sender, so it breaks whenever newOwner != caller.
For any address argument passed by the current owner, setOwner(newOwner) makes c.owner() exactly newOwner; the mutant instead always assigns msg.sender, so it breaks whenever newOwner != the caller.

For every admissible new owner address, calling setOwner(a) as the owner must make c.owner() equal exactly a; the mutant instead always sets the zero address, so it violates the rule for any nonzero a.

For any caller that is the current owner and any proposed address, calling setOwner(_owner) must set the stored owner to exactly _owner; the mutant never updates owner, so c.owner() != _owner for some fuzzed address.

For any caller who is the current owner and any address a, calling setOwner(a) must leave owner == a; the mutant instead sets owner to address(this), which differs from a for any fuzzed a != address(this).
